candidates.heuristic_context: Target problem types: heterogeneous cases processed in a uniform way, so simple cases carry the effort of complex ones. Applicable when cases with clearly different recorded characteristics all follow the same path.
candidates.additional_context: case:AMOUNT_REQ <= 5000 splits the log into 3798 and 9289 cases that are routed differently at 3 gateway(s), reaching 3 activities: 'A_CANCELLED', 'O_CREATED', 'O_SENT_BACK'. The mined model has no access to the attribute, so each of those gateways uses one pooled probability for every case — strongest example, NOT (case:AMOUNT_REQ <= 5000) reaches 'O_CREATED' 45% of the time against 23% for the rest (z=23.7), while the model sends 29% of arrivals there regardless. The redesign attaches the condition at every one of those gateways, so the case type is routed consistently rather than at a coin flip. ⚠️ The condition is a HARD predicate, so it sends 100% of this type to 'O_CREATED' and 0% of the rest, where the log shows 45% and 23% — 78 percentage points of standardisation beyond what the log already does, which is the intervention rather than a reproduction of it. ⚠️ This changes WHICH cases go where, not how long anything takes: no hours are assumed anywhere, and whether routing by type helps, hurts or does nothing is for the simulation to measure. ⚠️ Direction of the change: in the log a case that reaches 'O_CREATED' still records 7.0 further events and 0.500 h of further work, against 12.6 events and 1.097 h for an average case. Most of the case still lies ahead of it, so forcing this type through it ADDS work rather than removing it; there is no free KPI win in this direction.
